questions.question:
Convert the imperative sentence into Passive Voice:
'Switch off the server room air conditioners before leaving.'

options.text: Let the server room air conditioners be switched off before leaving.
The server room air conditioners were switched off before leaving.
Let the server room air conditioners switched off before leaving.
You should have switched off the server room air conditioners before leaving.

questions.explanation: Active sentence direct command/instruction hai jisme direct object 'the server room air conditioners' present hai. Transitive imperative sentence ka standard passive formula hota hai: 'Let + Object + be + V3'. Is formula ke anusar 'Let the server room air conditioners be switched off...' (A) bilkul sahi hai. Option (B) Simple Past assertive sentence bana deta hai jo galat hai. Option (C) mein auxiliary 'be' missing hai. Option (D) modal-perfect banakar original sentence structure ko distort karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-01: Transitive Imperatives = Let + Object + be + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the polite request into Passive Voice:
'Please upload the signed affidavit on the judicial portal.'

options.text: Let the signed affidavit be uploaded on the judicial portal please.
You are requested to upload the signed affidavit on the judicial portal.
You are ordered to upload the signed affidavit on the judicial portal.
The signed affidavit must have been uploaded on the judicial portal.

questions.explanation: Active sentence mein 'Please' laga hai, jo polite request express kar raha hai. Request wale imperative sentences ka passive standardly 'You are requested to + V1' se banta hai. Is construction mein 'Please' drop ho jata hai kyunki 'requested' uska sense already convey karta hai. Option (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (A) unnatural hai aur redundant 'please' retain karta hai. Option (C) harsh order bana deta hai jo speaker ki request tone se contradict karta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-02: Polite Requests = You are requested to + V1 + Object (drop 'please/kindly').
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the negative imperative into Passive Voice:
'Do not share the confidential database credentials.'

options.text: Let the confidential database credentials be not shared.
Let the confidential database credentials not be shared.
You are forbidden not to share the confidential database credentials.
The confidential database credentials should not share.

questions.explanation: Negative imperative 'Do not + V1 + Object' ka standard passive structure hota hai: 'Let + Object + not + be + V3'. Yahan 'not' hamesha auxiliary 'be' se theek pehle aana chahiye: 'not be shared' (B). Option (A) mein 'be not shared' inverted word order blunder hai. Option (C) mein 'forbidden' ke sath 'not' lagakar fatal double-negative error kiya gaya hai. Option (D) mein 'be' missing hai aur sentence active hi reh gaya hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-03: Negative Imperatives = Let + Object + not + be + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Choose the most appropriate passive conversion for the sentence:
'Help the flood victims with food and medicine.'

options.text: Let the flood victims be helped with food and medicine.
The flood victims should be helped with food and medicine.
You are commanded to help the flood victims with food and medicine.
Food and medicine must help the flood victims.

questions.explanation: Sentence kisi military command ya coercive order ka nahi hai, balki moral duty aur human compassion (salah/kartavya) ka hai. Moral obligation ya welfare advice wale imperatives mein 'Object + should be + V3' sabse natural aur preferred exam construction hoti hai: 'The flood victims should be helped...' (B). Option (A) grammatically possible hone ke bawajood advice ke context mein cold aur unnatural lagta hai. Option (C) command tone add karta hai jo inappropriate hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-04: Advice & Duty = Object + should be + V3.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The registry can issue a duplicate certified copy.'

options.text: A duplicate certified copy could be issued by the registry.
A duplicate certified copy can be issued by the registry.
A duplicate certified copy can be issuing by the registry.
A duplicate certified copy must be issued by the registry.

questions.explanation: Active sentence mein simple modal auxiliary 'can' hai. Simple modal passive ka formula hota hai: 'Object + Modal + be + V3 + (by + Subject)'. Modal 'can' freeze rahega aur 'can be issued' (B) banega. Option (A) modal ko 'could' mein backshift kar deta hai jo Narration ka rule hai (Voice mein modal freeze rehta hai). Option (C) mein 'issuing' present participle hai jabki passive mein hamesha V3 past participle aana chahiye. Option (D) modal ko 'must' mein badal deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-05: Simple Modal Passive = Object + Modal + be + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The committee should have submitted the report on time.'

options.text: The report should have been submitted by the committee on time.
The report should be submitted by the committee on time.
The report should have submitted by the committee on time.
The report should had been submitted by the committee on time.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Modal Perfect ('should have submitted') mein hai jo ek unfulfilled past duty darshata hai. Modal Perfect passive formula hota hai: 'Object + Modal + have been + V3 + (by + Subject)'. Isliye 'The report should have been submitted...' (A) bilkul accurate hai. Option (B) simple modal ('should be submitted') banakar past aspect kho deta hai. Option (C) mein 'been' missing hai jisse sentence active hi reh gaya. Option (D) mein 'had' laga diya gaya jo modal ke baad grammatically impossible hai (modal ke baad hamesha bare base 'have' aati hai).
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-06: Modal Perfect Passive = Object + Modal + have been + V3 + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the question into Passive Voice:
'Can the forensic expert recover the erased hard drive partitions?'

options.text: Can the erased hard drive partitions be recovered by the forensic expert?
Can be the erased hard drive partitions recovered by the forensic expert?
Could the erased hard drive partitions be recovered by the forensic expert?
The erased hard drive partitions can be recovered by the forensic expert?

questions.explanation: Active sentence modal question hai: 'Can + Subject + V1 + Object?'. Interrogative passive mein modal helping verb subject se pehle inverted position mein hi rahegi: 'Modal + Object + be + V3 + (by + Subject)?'. Isliye 'Can the erased hard drive partitions be recovered...?' (A) sahi hai. Option (B) mein 'Can be' dono helping verbs ko subject se pehle le aaya jo wrong word order hai. Option (C) modal ko 'could' mein backshift karta hai. Option (D) question inverted syntax ko todkar assertive word order bana deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-07: Interrogative Modal Passive = Modal + Object + be + V3 + (by + Subject)?
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The High Court committee is looking into the procedural irregularities.'

options.text: The procedural irregularities are being looked by the High Court committee.
The procedural irregularities are being looked into by the High Court committee.
The procedural irregularities were looked into by the High Court committee.
The procedural irregularities have been looked into by the High Court committee.

questions.explanation: 'Look into' ek prepositional verb hai jiska matlab 'investigate karna' hota hai. Preposition retention rule kehta hai ki preposition verb ke past participle ke theek baad chipki rahegi, chahe agent ke liye 'by' alag se lagana pade. Active sentence Present Continuous ('is looking into') mein hai aur naya subject plural ('irregularities') hai, isliye 'are being looked into by...' (B) sahi answer hai. Option (A) preposition 'into' ko drop kar deta hai jisse sentence ka meaning destroy ho jata hai. Option (C) Simple Past aur Option (D) Present Perfect hai jo tense freeze rule violate karte hain.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Prepositional Verbs = Object + be + V3 + Preposition + (by + Subject). Preposition drop nahi hogi!
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'Everyone laughed at his strange argument in the court.'

options.text: His strange argument was laughed by everyone in the court.
His strange argument was laughed at by everyone in the court.
His strange argument had been laughed at by everyone in the court.
His strange argument is laughed at by everyone in the court.

questions.explanation: 'Laugh at' prepositional verb hai. Active verb Simple Past ('laughed at') mein hai. Passive form mein auxiliary 'was' aayegi aur preposition 'at' verb ke sath retain rahegi: 'was laughed at by everyone' (B). Yahan 'at by' do prepositions ek sath aana grammatically perfectly valid hai ('at' verb ka part hai aur 'by' agent marker hai). Option (A) mein 'at' missing hai jo fatal error hai. Option (C) Past Perfect bana deta hai aur Option (D) Simple Present bana deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-08: Prepositional Verbs = Object + was/were + V3 + at + by + Subject.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice:
'The transport union has called off the statewide bus strike.'

options.text: The statewide bus strike has called off by the transport union.
The statewide bus strike has been called off by the transport union.
The statewide bus strike was called off by the transport union.
The statewide bus strike has been called by the transport union.

questions.explanation: Active sentence Present Perfect ('has called off') mein hai aur 'call off' transitive phrasal verb hai (meaning: cancel karna). Present Perfect passive formula hota hai: 'Object + has/have been + V3 + particle'. Naya subject singular ('The statewide bus strike') hai, isliye 'has been called off by...' (B) bilkul sahi hai. Option (A) mein 'been' missing hai. Option (C) Simple Past kar deta hai. Option (D) particle 'off' ko drop kar deta hai jisse strike cancel hone ki jagah bulaaye jaane ka ulta meaning ban jata hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-09: Phrasal Verbs = Object + be + V3 + Particle + (by + Subject). Particle intact rahega.
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice by promoting the Indirect Object (Person):
'The administrative judge gave the court assistant a commendation letter.'

options.text: A commendation letter was given the court assistant by the administrative judge.
The court assistant was given a commendation letter by the administrative judge.
The court assistant was gave a commendation letter by the administrative judge.
A commendation letter was given to the court assistant by the administrative judge.

questions.explanation: Active sentence mein do objects hain: Indirect Object (Person) = 'the court assistant', aur Direct Object (Thing) = 'a commendation letter'. Question mein specifically Indirect Object ko promote karne ko kaha gaya hai. Jab Indirect Object subject banta hai, toh formula hota hai: 'IO + was/were + V3 + Direct Object + by-agent'. Isliye 'The court assistant was given a commendation letter...' (B) bilkul accurate hai. Option (D) Direct Object promote karta hai (halanki grammatically correct hai, par question ki requirement IO promote karne ki thi). Option (A) mein 'to' missing hai. Option (C) mein V2 'gave' lagaya hai jo galat hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Two-Object Passives = IO + be + V3 + Direct Object + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05

questions.question:
Convert the sentence into Passive Voice by promoting the Direct Object (Thing):
'The registry sent the appellant an urgent reminder.'

options.text: An urgent reminder was sent the appellant by the registry.
An urgent reminder was sent to the appellant by the registry.
The appellant was sent an urgent reminder by the registry.
An urgent reminder had been sent to the appellant by the registry.

questions.explanation: Jab Direct Object ('An urgent reminder') ko passive subject banaya jata hai, toh Indirect Object (person) se pehle preposition 'to' lagana compulsory hota hai: 'DO + was/were + V3 + TO + IO + (by + Subject)'. Isliye 'An urgent reminder was sent to the appellant by the registry' (B) sahi answer hai. Option (A) preposition 'to' ko drop kar deta hai jo classic fatal error hai. Option (C) Indirect Object ko promote karta hai, jabki question mein Direct Object ko promote karne ko kaha gaya hai. Option (D) tense ko Past Perfect kar deta hai.
questions.ruleReference: Rule RC-10: Promoting Direct Object = DO + be + V3 + to/for + IO + (by + Subject).
questions.provenanceSource: Authored for HSA EnglishMaster Module L05
